metadata.title: "Verified" Isn't Evidence.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: an agent's 'verified' is a claim, not evidence; the artifact you name before the task starts is what makes it checkable. Lands the carry-out that the evidence artifact, named up front, is what makes an output verifiable instead of just claimed.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B06 (the four-field verification-protocol card: planted filled for a research task, returns filled for a code task, same four boxes)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes an agent's 'verified' means the claim is true. But verified only means something you can check — an artifact you name before the task starts. So: does verified mean true, or checkable?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'The agent says it's verified. Verified means true. Right?', hesitates on 'true', corrects to 'checkable'

props.text:
The agent says
it's verified.
Verified means true.
Right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. Single-word trigger ('true') swapped for a single-word replacement ('checkable') so buildActs()'s whitespace-token match fires (per the constitution-redo lesson on multi-word triggers). TIMING LAW: 33-word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('true' -> 'checkable') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Before an agent starts a task, ask it to generate a verification protocol: the output type, the independent evidence that would confirm it worked, the specific check for the likeliest failure, and the artifact that has to exist afterward. On a citation-summary task: evidence is a source map — which file backs which claim.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - a four-field verification protocol card filled for a research task

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - the four-field protocol
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labeled OUTPUT TYPE, INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE, KEY CHECK, REQUIRED ARTIFACT, filled in one at a time for a research task: research summary / source map / open the cited documents / file-to-claim map. THIS EXACT FOUR-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B06.

beats.narration_text: The natural shortcut: the agent already read every source once, so ask it to reread its own summary and confirm the citations hold. If it says 'verified,' that should be enough.

shot.new_visual_element: The agent's own output looping back into a self-check, ending in a VERIFIED stamp

production_viz.label: The natural guess - ask it to check itself
production_viz.mechanic: A document icon feeds into a loop arrow that curls back into the same document icon, labeled 'SELF-CHECK'. The loop closes with a large stamp reading VERIFIED landing on top.

beats.narration_text: But that check runs on the same reasoning that wrote the summary — a citation matched against the agent's own training data instead of the actual paper can get re-confirmed as 'verified' by the exact same process. Independent evidence has to come from outside the agent's own say-so: open the cited document yourself.

shot.new_visual_element: The self-check loop struck through; an independent artifact standing apart, unconnected

production_viz.label: The break - the loop can't catch its own error
production_viz.mechanic: The B02 self-check card reappears, now struck through in terracotta. Beside it, physically separated with no arrow connecting them, a document icon labeled 'THE ACTUAL PAPER' — the only thing outside the loop.

beats.narration_text: That's why the protocol gets designed before the agent starts, not after it finishes: name the output type and the required artifact first, and 'verified' always cashes out to something you can go check, not just a word the agent used.

shot.new_visual_element: A timeline: the protocol card appears before TASK STARTS, not after TASK DONE

production_viz.label: Designed before, not checked after
production_viz.mechanic: A horizontal timeline with two gates: 'TASK STARTS' on the left, 'TASK DONE' on the right. The four-field protocol card sits directly beside the left gate, with an arrow pointing forward through the whole timeline; a faded, struck-through copy of the same card sits after 'TASK DONE' to show the rejected order.

beats.narration_text: A checked artifact only proves what its specific check covers — the source map proves every claim traces to a real document, not that the summary's interpretation of those documents is fair or complete.

shot.new_visual_element: The source-map artifact, checked inside its boundary; a faded box outside reading 'interpretation is fair'

production_viz.label: A pass only proves what it checks
production_viz.mechanic: A bounded box labeled 'CHECKED: traces to a document' with a checkmark inside it, drawn around the source-map artifact. Outside the box's dashed boundary, a separate faded card reads 'interpretation is fair' with no checkmark — visibly untouched by the check.

beats.narration_text: And an artifact that looks different isn't a verdict on the agent generally — reapply the exact same four-field card to a code change, and the fills swap entirely: evidence becomes running the tests and reading the diff, the artifact becomes that test output plus the diff. Same structure, an independent check, every time.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - the same four-box card, filled for a code task

production_viz.label: The anchor returns - same card, new fill
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 FOUR-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical layout. Each card's fill swaps in turn: OUTPUT TYPE -> code change, INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE -> run tests / inspect diff, KEY CHECK -> diff shows only intended changes, REQUIRED ARTIFACT -> test output + diff. The research-task fills from B01 fade beneath as faint ghosts, showing the swap.

beats.narration_text: An agent's 'verified' is a claim, not evidence — the artifact you name before the task starts is what makes it checkable.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want to build an independent verification protocol for an agent output in my workflow. Walk me through the protocol structure: what makes verification genuinely independent rather than just re-checking the same way? What classes of error does each check catch — and what does the minimum viable protocol look like for a high-stakes output? Liam, in for Bear.
